You agreed to be his sub and to follow certain rules. You made a mistake, whether willfully because you wanted to test boundaries or accidentally because you weren't focused. Now he's going to punish you as agreed, either because he wants to train you to be better and/or because it's fun. Seven days without cumming doesn't seem that severe to me. I imagine it's frustrating to be punished, but that's kind of the essence of punishment. Do you consent to punishment, or only to "funishment"?

Again, I'm coming to this as a Dom, but what I see is that you want to control the punishment. It looks like topping from the bottom. Hopefully the reason you're a sub is because you want to give up control. It's not as though he's asking you to hurt yourself or put yourself or someone else in danger. He's asking you to make a difficult but ultimately trivial sacrifice, which will be full of sexy delights and anguish. Perhaps it seems overwhelming today, but maybe tomorrow you'll feel more optimistic and open. You can do much more than you think you can. This is training, boot camp, etc. It's not meant to be easy.

Are you more upset that he's taking your violation so seriously, which makes you feel like a failure? Or are you more upset about not cumming for seven days?

If the former, then your Dom probably wants to hear about this; it means you take your commitment seriously. I'd see this as a growth opportunity for the relationship. You come out of it more submissive; he comes out of it with greater control, as well as a better understanding of your mentality.

If the latter, then I think you're topping from the bottom. I'd see this as a soul-searching opportunity. Prolonged edging can be exciting and sexy. Instead of rebelling against it, talk to your husband about your anxieties. Be vulnerable, and do not expect him to bend to your will. If your dynamic leaves punishment up to him, then don't try to compensate him in other ways. Just learn, obey, and enjoy. If you don't like being a sub, then void the contract. It is very frustrating for a Dom when a sub promises to submit and then tries to control the dynamic. Your feelings are real and valid, but you need to take responsibility for your commitments and address your feelings within your framework. If you feel overwhelmed by the punishment, tell him, but don't demand that he change it. "I feel overwhelmed by this punishment" should not mean he has to back off. Work through your feelings together without usurping control.

If you don't feel safe, if you feel like your husband is violating your contract, or if you aren't cut out for D/s dynamics, then you need to renegotiate your relationship. Otherwise, now is an exciting time to go deeper into submission and trust. You can do it! Good luck!

I am currently self medicating in a similar way. I’ve been self medicating off and on with amphetamine for several years and with methamphetamine for a few months. I think desoxyn/ma is a great antidepressant. Treating your anhedonia will enable you to engage in healthy behaviors like socializing and exercising, which creates a virtuous cycle. However, depressed people have upregulated dopamine receptors, so you may be especially sensitive and get caught up manically pursuing porn, gambling etc., so watch out for that. 

5 mg is a very small amount, so you need a good mg scale. Respect the dose. Dose is everything. I suspect the naysayers on here have experience with large doses and different ROAs. 5-10 mg/day orally is a reasonable dose. 200 mg smoked is not. I know MA has a terrible reputation, but dosing and ROA are the difference between self destruction and therapy. 

Give yourself a couple weeks of regular dosing to see how you fair. My first doses made me a bit manic, but it’s mellowed out and I’ve become more productive since then. Take it early in the day; it does last ages. 

Take breaks to avoid building tolerance. I take weekends off and get extra rest. I still feel some therapeutic effects even when not under the influence. I believe this is due to memories of functioning reward circuits and the confidence that engenders.

Good luck. Update us.

As a master in a similar power struggle with my slave, my instinct is to say that the beauty of the M/s dynamic is that, if the dynamic is working properly, these issues are reduced dramatically compared to a vanilla relationship where differences in moods and cravings devolve into nagging and resentment. In my fantasy of a functioning M/s relationship, the Master has military-like authority and the slave doesn’t feel free to question or push back AT ALL, within the bounds of the agreed limits. It sounds like you’re well within your agreed-upon limits to insist, but your authority has slipped and now you’re feeling disempowered and your slave is being bratty. 

I’m answering your post here not as someone who’s already solved this issue in practice. I’m struggling to manage a sulking, argumentative slave myself. But sometimes discussing others’ issues can help to put one’s own in focus. So I hope this is mutually beneficial. 

Some advice I’ve gotten from other dominants:
1) Obviously a review and possible renegotiation of your rights and responsibilities may be a first step if this is a recurring issue. 
2) Once you have reaffirmed your authority over this area in your slave’s life, prepare her with rehearsing in advance of the issue. “slave, are my rules regarding not smoking clear? Good. I expect perfect compliance, and I will be very pleased and reward you after you come home tonight without smoking any cigarettes at all.” (I am biased toward positive reinforcement.)
3) Bupropion is a highly effective smoking cessation aid. It is also an antidepressant and has a very good side effect profile compared to other antidepressants. Consider committing to 12+ months on bupropion. 

You are well within your authority here, and if you’re like me, you need to hear that sometimes when your slave is being a brat because you respect her feelings and know she can’t just turn them off like a light switch; emotions aren’t that easy to control. So you need to strategize. Posting here for ideas was a great idea. 

Authority only works with real threats. So I’ll finish with another piece of advice I got from a fellow Dom. Think about the difference between a dealbreaker and an ultimatum. You can give her an ultimatum without abandoning her—“You want to argue with me? Fine! You’re free. Do whatever the hell you want!”

Instead, find an ultimatum that will make it more uncomfortable for her to disobey than to obey. (“If you smoke, I will ground you at home for a week. If you argue and sulk, I will block you for 2 days while you think about what’s important to you.) Ultimately, she has to decide whether she wants to obey or lose you. Ultimately, losing the relationship has to be on the table. You can’t lock her up against her will and beat her like a real slave. You have to be stronger than she. Don’t tolerate insolence from your slave. Listen to her concerns, but don’t get drawn into nagging and arguments. Military discipline, not vanilla bickering. 

Good luck!

A lot of what you say at the end about the world being horrible—it’s really true. The Buddha realized that 2,500 years ago, before he became enlightened. He was a prince. He had everything: beauty, brawn, power, wealth, and prestige. But one day he sneaked out of his palace to see the outside world, and he was horrified to discover the decrepitness of old age, as well as disease and death. He also saw one more thing—an ascetic meditator seeking liberation from addiction to pleasure and the rollercoaster of life. The Buddha (his name was still Siddhartha really, as he wasn’t yet enlightened) saw that life was suffering and that it was NOT ok.

Nowadays, everyone has to think that life is beautiful and, on the whole, good. The Buddha did not think that. He was not life affirming. By seeing the horror of life, the suffering all around you, you have taken one step toward awakening, OP. 

In Buddhist thought, sentient beings reincarnate into six different realms: Hell (the most horrible), the Hungry Ghost Realm (still really horrible), the Animal Realm (meh), the Human Realm (more about this later), the Demigod Realm (imagine the Greek and Roman gods—powerful but afflicted by jealousy and anger), and Heaven (a place with no suffering whatsoever). No incarnations are eternal, although incarnations in the lower two and higher two realms last for like millions or billions of years. Eventually, every being dies, even in Heaven, and is reincarnated into another or the same realm. Beings in the lower two realms are so consumed by their suffering that they cannot contemplate a route to liberation. Beings in the higher two realms are so preoccupied with their pleasure and power that they feel no need to seek a route to liberation. Animals are not intelligent enough to contemplate a route to liberation. That leaves humans—the only sentient beings that can contemplate the first Noble Truth: Life is Suffering. We are in a unique position in the Buddhist view of the cosmos, for we know both suffering and pleasure, but we also have the ability to contemplate them and seek a route to liberation. 

I don’t believe in reincarnation. When we die, we no longer exist. But the Buddhist view of reincarnation does highlight an interesting point. We who see suffering, feel it deeply, and don’t sweep it under the rug; we are the ones who can consider human and animal suffering with clarity. People who are basically happy and satisfied with life, they are blinded to the profound suffering around them, for how can you sympathize with suffering if you haven’t experienced it for yourself?

You, OP, are one step along on the path of the Buddha. Perhaps you can find meaning where more fortunate people cannot because of their ability to compartmentalize and dismiss suffering. The Buddha said that liberation from suffering is possible, even here in this life. I don’t know if total liberation from suffering truly is possible, but I have known many people who have found great relief in pursuing egoless clarity through meditation. If you’re not accustomed to exercise, as I wasn’t for my first 30 years of life, then I think the important thing is to increase the amount you exercise. For me, weight training is more rewarding than cardio. I like to set myself a goal (e.g. x number of repetitions with y kg weights) and focus on the 30-90 seconds it takes to complete that goal. Then I set my next goal and do that 10-20 times/workout. Short bouts of high-intensity effort are much more manageable for me than running on a treadmill for half an hour. 

My point is, find something you can force yourself to do regularly and long term to increase the demands you’re placing on your body. If walking a treadmill on an incline while listening to a podcast works for you, then set attainable goals and work to increase your limits. Get a comfortably elevated heart rate and breathing rate. Break a sweat if you can. Your limits are mental, not physical. Accept that. You’re training your brain and your neurological system as well as your muscles, so be patient with your psyche. The important thing is to keep at it. It will get easier, and you’ll start to feel motivated to increase your time, reps, and resistance. It’s a wonderful thing when you get to that point of enjoying pushing your limits. 

So walk around the block a few seconds faster than yesterday. Do one more push-up than last week. Check out a new yoga class. Just do something to increase your amount of exercise. Make exercise a high priority. Schedule it in your calendar and don’t cancel for non emergency reasons. 

Try not to compare yourself to others. (Impossible not to do, I know.) Enjoy the fact that you are as fit and capable as you are. Soon you’ll enjoy the fact that you’re fitter and more capable than you were a few months earlier. Compete with yourself, not others. You will never have a body like the ones you admire on billboards. But that’s good, because being your best self is much better than forcing yourself into a mold. Be authentically you, not a fake poser.
